areas.summary: RawDrive authenticates platform users with an RS256-signed JWT access token plus an opaque, rotating, family-tracked refresh token. Four mint paths exist: password Login (handler.go:425), email-OTP activation VerifyOTP (handler.go:521, registration-only), Google OAuth callback (handler.go:697), and MFA step-up VerifyTOTP/VerifyRecoveryCode (mfa_handler.go:395/517). All access tokens carry sub, workspace_id, role (workspace), platform_role, state_id, and mfa_verified, bound to iss/aud "rawdrive-api" (auth.go:33-36). Refresh sessions persist the same claim set plus mfa_verified to a DB-backed store (refresh_sessions, migrations 062/064) so rotation never silently downgrades MFA state, and the RSA signing key persists across restarts (jwt_key_persistence.go). MFA is opt-in TOTP step-up: requiresMFAStepUp (handler.go:682) is the shared gate for both password Login and OAuth callback, so OAuth cannot skip the second factor. Fresh users (password or Google) get workspace_id="pending-onboarding" claims and are routed to /onboarding by the frontend (auth.ts:170), where the workspace + plan_tier are actually created (onboarding.go:198). Platform users use the rawdrive-api JWT audience via middleware.JWTAuth; gallery viewers use a wholly separate viewer-session JWT verified by streaming/viewer.Service in middleware/viewer_context.go, never the platform key. OAuth state is HMAC-signed with the Google client secret (auth.go:776) carrying nonce/returnTo/expiry. The Google OAuth signup path produces a functionally usable account (user row + linked auth method) but NOT a field-complete one relative to password Register, and the OAuth state has replay weaknesses — detailed below.

areas.outwardContracts: Hands the rest of the platform an RS256 JWT (iss=aud="rawdrive-api") whose claims are the tenancy contract: workspace_id is THE tenant key consumed by middleware.TenantContext (sets current_workspace_id for RLS), role is the workspace RBAC level, platform_role drives RequirePlatformRole, state_id drives RequireState. middleware.JWTAuth mirrors sub into claims["user_id"] because downstream handlers (gallery duplication created_by, design-collab presence/locks, templates) read user_id directly. A fresh user is handed workspace_id="pending-onboarding" + state_id="pending-onboarding" and is expected to pass through the Onboarding area (onboarding.go) which performs the real workspaces row + plan_tier + workspace_members writes; only after that does RefreshToken/Login resolve real claims via workspace.AuthLookup.GetUserWorkspace. Identity expected inbound from Storage/Upload/Gallery areas: a platform Bearer JWT for owner operations; gallery viewers instead present the separate viewer-session JWT (viewer_context.go) which carries NO workspace_id/tenant context by design. Billing/Plans area is fed via PlanTierLookup.GetWorkspacePlanTier keyed on workspace_id.

areas.summary: The word "customer" maps to three distinct concepts. (a) Platform users = photographers, in the `users` table (migration 002_create_users) served by `backend/internal/user/` (user.go, repo.go, auth_adapter.go); identity = JWT `sub`. (b) The photographer's CRM clients/contacts/leads/deals, in `contacts` (contact_type IN client|vendor|collaborator), `leads`, and `deals` (migration 021_create_m4_crm_tables), served by `backend/internal/handler/{contact,lead,deal,client_profile,contact_import}_handler.go`; all are workspace-scoped via RLS (`app.workspace_id`) plus the `getWorkspaceID()` helper. (c) Gallery/stream viewers — there is NO dedicated viewer entity; gallery viewers are email-keyed activity rows (client_conversations, proofing_selections, gallery_access_logs, gallery_orders, download_events, etc.) joined to galleries by lowercased email (client_profile_handler.go:467-561), gallery proofing access is a password->gallery_session cookie token (gallery_access_handler.go), and live-stream viewers use a SEPARATE viewer-JWT audience via middleware/viewer_context.go. Tenancy: a user relates to a workspace as OWNER (workspaces.owner_id) AND via a workspace_members row (role_id->roles Owner/Admin/Editor/Viewer); AuthLookup.GetUserWorkspace prefers the membership join and falls back to the owner query (auth_lookup.go:27-71), so the system tolerates a missing membership row. The canonical lifecycle is: register (auth/handler.go Register) creates ONLY the users row + email OTP; the workspace, workspace_members, and workspace_storage quota row are created together LATER, exactly once, in onboarding SetProfile -> onboardingWorkspaceCreator.CreateWorkspace (cmd/api/main.go:460-532). Plan tier attaches to workspaces.plan_tier (default "free" because the onboarding handler forces paid selections to free, handler.go:117-121, until payment), and quota attaches via workspace_storage.quota_bytes seeded from service.PlanDefaultQuotaBytes. Onboarding state lives in the onboarding_statuses table (migration 067), NOT in the legacy users.onboarding_step column. Until onboarding completes the JWT carries workspace_id="pending-onboarding" (auth/handler.go:452), which getWorkspaceID() rejects so CRM/data routes are inert pre-onboarding.

areas.area: Uploader pipeline (chunked TUS + direct multipart → storage → asset row → WebP derivatives → gallery)
areas.summary: RawDrive has two upload entry points. (1) The primary chunked/TUS path: frontend `use-upload.ts` screens the file locally, POSTs `/api/v1/uploads` (CreateSession), PATCHes 5 MiB chunks straight to B2 multipart (no local disk), and finalizes when offset≥total_size. CreateSession reserves storage quota (`reserved_bytes`) and an upload credit (1/upload) before opening the B2 multipart; finalize composes the object, verifies the SHA-256/header-trailer, inserts the `assets` row with `status='processing'`, commits the storage reservation into `used_bytes`, and consumes the credit. (2) A direct multipart path `POST /api/v1/assets` via `UploadService` for smaller uploads. Neither upload path generates WebP derivatives synchronously, and neither publishes a NATS job — derivative/EXIF generation is driven ENTIRELY by the polling `ThumbnailWorker` (1s poll of `assets WHERE status='processing'`), which calls `ThumbnailService.GenerateAll` (4 concurrent cwebp variants), writes `asset_derivatives` rows, bumps `workspace_storage.derivative_bytes`, sets dimensions/blurhash/EXIF, and flips status to `ready`. Gallery/album association is NOT part of either upload — it happens client-side after completion via `addAssetToGallery` in the gallery page effect. Credit lifecycle is reserve→consume→refund with a TTL safety net (`ExpireAbandoned`) that is documented but NOT actually wired as a worker. The `ProcessingPipeline` NATS orchestrator exists but is unused in main.go.

Storage quota accounting via reserved_bytes: ReserveUpload at session create, CommitUploadReservation at finalize, ReleaseUploadReservation on cancel

Async WebP derivative generation (thumb_sm/md/lg_webp + display_webp 2400px) via polling ThumbnailWorker + cwebp, with asset_derivatives rows and derivative_bytes accounting

areas.outwardContracts: Identity in: both upload handlers read platform-user identity via middleware.JWTClaimsFromContext (getUserID → sub claim) and tenancy via middleware.WorkspaceIDFromContext (getWorkspaceID). Viewer-JWT (client gallery) audience cannot reach upload routes — uploads are photographer/platform-only. Ownership assumptions: the asset row carries workspace_id from the session/context and is the tenancy key; the upload pipeline assumes the asset will later be linked to a gallery in the SAME workspace, but the upload itself never receives or validates a gallery_id (no gallery_id column on upload_sessions). Hands outward: it emits an assets row in status='processing' (tenancy-scoped) that the AI/face/search subsystems and the gallery subsystem consume; gallery attachment is a separate POST /api/v1/galleries/{id}/assets call (handled by the GALLERY area) which validates gallery-in-workspace but NOT asset-in-workspace. To the BILLING/credits area it hands a reserve ledger entry per session keyed by upload_session_id, expecting that area's (currently-missing) ExpireAbandoned worker to settle drops. To the STORAGE/dashboard area it hands committed used_bytes (originals) at finalize and derivative_bytes later from the worker.

areas.area: GALLERY (gallery CRUD, sub-galleries/albums, asset listing & derivative serving, proofing, favorites, share links, public/viewer access, FaceID gate, downloads, branding/design, analytics)
areas.summary: A gallery belongs to a workspace (galleries.workspace_id) and is created/owned via the JWT-protected /api/v1/galleries group (JWTAuth + TenantContext middleware in main.go:1558-1559). The canonical GalleryHandler correctly enforces tenancy via requireGalleryInWorkspace, which loads the gallery and compares gallery.WorkspaceID against the request's workspace (gallery_handler.go:115-131). AlbumHandler follows the same discipline (album_handler.go:23-57, GalleryBelongsToWorkspace / GetByIDForWorkspace). However, the many gallery SUB-RESOURCE handlers added across M12-M14/M22 (access control, design, cover, share links, proofing, proofing sessions/comments, favorites, analytics, downloads, banners) take the {id}/{galleryId} straight from the URL and pass it to services that query only by gallery_id with NO workspace predicate and NO ownership re-check. Because share_links/proofing_selections/etc. have only gallery_id columns (no workspace_id — migrations 014, 015, 041), the sole isolation boundary would be a JOIN to galleries.workspace_id, which is absent throughout these chains. This produces a broad, systemic cross-tenant IDOR surface: an authenticated user in workspace A can read/modify another workspace's gallery passwords, share links, proofing selections, comments, analytics, download audit logs, and banners by supplying the victim's gallery/sub-resource UUID. On the public side, the viewer path (public_gallery_handler.go) gates assets ONLY on gallery.IsPublished plus an optional gallery-level password session (in-memory map); the per-gallery access_mode (private/invite-only, migration 041:102, default 'private') and share-link PIN/expiry/access-count (share_link_service.ValidateAccess) are never consulted by the asset-listing/download endpoints, so any published gallery is fully readable by slug regardless of access_mode or share-link protection. FaceID/People endpoints are correctly gallery-scoped (FindSimilarFacesInGallery / ListClusterAssetIDsInGallery) and double-gated on workspace + per-gallery flags. The authenticated edge-delivery endpoint serves any asset's WebP derivative by asset UUID with no gallery/workspace check at all.

seamFlows.seam: S1: OAuth identity → user record → workspace/plan/onboarding provisioning
seamFlows.flowDescription:
FIRST Google login vs FIRST password Register, traced against source:

PASSWORD REGISTER (backend/internal/auth/handler.go:339 Register): validates email+password+phone, FindByEmail pre-check for duplicate, then h.users.Create(email,password,fullName,phone,stateID,district) which persists state_id and a bcrypt password_hash with email_verified=FALSE (user/repo.go:46). It then sends an activation OTP and returns 201 with NO tokens. The user is NOT logged in and has NO workspace. Workspace is created later during onboarding.SetProfile (onboarding/onboarding.go:198 → wsc.CreateWorkspace), after the user activates via /auth/verify-otp (which flips email_verified=true and mints tokens with the still-"pending-onboarding" workspace). Login (handler.go:425) refuses unverified accounts with 403 (handler.go:446-448).

FIRST GOOGLE LOGIN (auth.go:702 HandleGoogleCallback): consumeState (HMAC-signed, see auth.go:807) → provider.ExchangeCode → provider.GetProfile (google_provider.go:72, decodes sub/email/name/picture — NOT email_verified). FindByEmail(profile.Email): if no row, OAuthService creates one via oauth_store.go:42 Create → user.Create(CreateUserInput{Email: record.Email}) ONLY — no password_hash (nil), no phone, no state_id (nil), email_verified defaults FALSE. Then LinkOAuth inserts a (user_id, provider, provider_subject) row into user_auth_methods (oauth_store.go:84). Back in the handler (handler.go:728-746), oauthWsID defaults to "pending-onboarding" and is overwritten by h.workspaces.GetUserWorkspace(user.ID) — so OAuth DOES run the same WorkspaceLookup as Login (workspace/auth_lookup.go:27). For a brand-new Google user with no workspace, GetUserWorkspace returns ("","","",platformRole,nil) (auth_lookup.go:63-68), so claims stay workspace_id="pending-onboarding", role="Owner", platform_role="photographer". requiresMFAStepUp is checked (handler.go:755) keeping parity with Login. The handler then mints ONLY a refresh token (handler.go:779 GenerateRefreshTokenWithClaims) — NO access token — sets the refresh cookie and 302-redirects to the frontend with ?authenticated=1.

The frontend LoginForm (LoginForm.tsx:81-103) sees authenticated=1 and calls refreshAuthSession → POST /auth/refresh, which RotateRefreshToken issues an access token AND re-resolves workspace from DB (handler.go:814-839); for the new user this is still pending-onboarding. getPostLoginPath (frontend/src/lib/auth.ts:170-173) and the dashboard layout (layout.tsx:358) both route workspace_id=="pending-onboarding" to /onboarding. The user completes onboarding (state + profile), SetProfile creates the workspace, and the NEXT /auth/refresh upgrades workspace_id to the real id (handler.go:820). Until onboarding completes, getWorkspaceID (handler/asset_handler.go:261) rejects "pending-onboarding", so upload CreateSession / gallery create / album / contacts etc. return not-authorized — exactly as they do for a freshly-activated password user. So the pending-onboarding provisioning path is symmetric and correctly wired between OAuth and password flows.

CONCLUSION ON THE CORE WIRING: OAuthGoogleCallback DOES run WorkspaceLookup before issuing the token (contrary to the worry in the prompt), MFA step-up parity is preserved, and the empty-workspace user is funnelled to onboarding identically to a new password user. The dangerous-sounding "empty workspace_id token" is the intended pending-onboarding state, not a gap. The real defects are in (a) account-linking/email-verification trust and (b) the user_auth_methods table being write-only with no uniqueness, plus minor inconsistencies.
workingWell: OAuthGoogleCallback runs h.workspaces.GetUserWorkspace before minting tokens (handler.go:732-746), so a Google user who already has a workspace gets correct workspace_id/role/platform_role/state_id claims — same resolver Login uses (handler.go:457).

New-user 'pending-onboarding' fallback is identical across Login (handler.go:452-455), VerifyOTP (handler.go:552-555), and OAuth (handler.go:728-731); getWorkspaceID rejects 'pending-onboarding' uniformly (asset_handler.go:261) and the frontend routes it to /onboarding (auth.ts:172, layout.tsx:358).

Post-onboarding token upgrade is wired: /auth/refresh re-resolves the real workspace from DB and regenerates the access token while preserving mfa_verified (handler.go:814-838), so the pending-onboarding claim self-heals after onboarding completes.
MFA step-up parity: OAuth callback calls the same requiresMFAStepUp gate (handler.go:755, 682) as password Login (handler.go:481), so an enrolled user cannot bypass TOTP by using Google.

OAuth state CSRF is HMAC-SHA256 signed with the client secret and carries a 10-minute expiry (auth.go:677-699, 807-839); the signed-state path is stateless so it survives multi-instance deployments (proven by TestGoogleOAuth_StateSurvivesBackendInstanceSwitch).

OAuth is only wired when all of GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/REDIRECT_URL are present (main.go:992), so in production ClientSecret is always set and state signing is always active — the unsigned in-memory fallback only triggers in tests with no secret.
Profile backfill is guarded: existing display_name/avatar are only overwritten when currently empty (auth.go:731-743), so Google data never clobbers user-edited profile fields.

OAuth callback issues a refresh-only response by design and the frontend correctly exchanges it for an access token via refreshAuthSession (LoginForm.tsx:87) — the absence of an access token in the redirect is intentional, not broken.

seamFlows.seam: S2: user/workspace → gallery ownership & tenant isolation
seamFlows.flowDescription:
Owner-side requests enter through the authenticated router group in backend/cmd/api/main.go:1557-1648 (`r.Group` → `JWTAuth` → `TenantContext` → `PlanTierContext`), which mounts `handler.RegisterM2Routes(api, ...)`. workspace_id is taken from JWT claims (not client input): middleware.TenantContext (backend/internal/middleware/middleware.go:118) reads `claims["workspace_id"]` and stashes it via the typed context key, and getWorkspaceID (backend/internal/handler/asset_handler.go:258) reads it back through middleware.WorkspaceIDFromContext — so the tenancy key itself is trustworthy.

Tenant isolation is intended to be enforced in two layers: (a) Postgres RLS policies (migrations 008 + 061) keyed on `current_setting('app.workspace_id')`, set per-request by middleware.PgDBContext.SetWorkspaceID (backend/internal/middleware/db_context.go:29); and (b) application-layer workspace_id predicates/ownership checks in handlers and repos. Crucially, layer (a) is INERT in production: the app connects as the DB-owning role `rawdrive` (docker-compose POSTGRES_USER / DATABASE_URL in .env.cobolt:12, .env.backend:1), which BYPASSES RLS because no migration sets `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` — RLS is only exercised in tests via `SET ROLE rawdrive_app` (backend/internal/database/test_helpers.go:82). Additionally SetWorkspaceID runs `set_config(..., is_local=false)` on a pooled connection via `pool.Exec`, then the connection returns to the pool, so a subsequent repo query on a different pooled connection would not even carry the session var. Net effect: isolation depends ENTIRELY on layer (b), the per-handler workspace_id checks.

Gallery and Album object routes implement layer (b) correctly. GalleryHandler.requireGalleryInWorkspace (backend/internal/handler/gallery_handler.go:115-131) loads the gallery and rejects when `gallery.WorkspaceID != workspaceID`; every gallery object route (GetByID/Update/SoftDelete/AddAsset/RemoveAsset/ReorderAssets/Timeline/ListAssets/TriggerFaceScan/SetFaceDetection/Duplicate) calls it, and gallery_authorization_source_test.go pins this invariant. AlbumHandler uses requireAlbumInWorkspace / requireGalleryInWorkspace (album_handler.go:23-57) backed by AlbumService.GalleryBelongsToWorkspace (album_service.go:113). The repos (gallery_repo.go, album_repo.go, gallery_asset_repo.go, proofing_repo.go, share_link_repo.go) are themselves unscoped (queries key only on id / gallery_id), which is acceptable ONLY because the handler enforces ownership first — so any handler that forgets the check is a direct IDOR.

Several sibling owner-side routes mounted under the SAME `/api/v1/galleries/{id}/...` tree skip the ownership helper entirely: share links (routes_m2.go:155-157 → share_link_handler.go), proofing selections and sessions (routes_m2.go:160-199 → proofing_handler.go / proofing_session_handler.go), and gallery analytics (routes_m2.go:321-327 → gallery_analytics_handler.go). The standalone asset routes (routes_m2.go:73-75) and the asset-link writes (AddAsset/AddAssets) also lack per-object workspace verification. Because RLS does not backstop them in production, each is a cross-workspace IDOR reachable by any authenticated user guessing/enumerating IDs.
workingWell: Gallery object routes are workspace-scoped: GalleryHandler.requireGalleryInWorkspace (gallery_handler.go:115-131) compares the loaded gallery.WorkspaceID against the JWT-derived workspace and returns 404, and every gallery CRUD/asset route calls it (gallery_handler.go GetByID/Update/SoftDelete/AddAsset/RemoveAsset/ReorderAssets/Timeline/ListAssets/TriggerFaceScan).

Album object routes are workspace-scoped via AlbumService.GalleryBelongsToWorkspace / GetByIDForWorkspace (album_service.go:113-136) called by AlbumHandler.requireAlbumInWorkspace / requireGalleryInWorkspace (album_handler.go:23-57).

workspace_id is sourced from JWT claims, never a client-supplied body/query value: middleware.TenantContext (middleware.go:118) + getWorkspaceID (asset_handler.go:258). The URL-based /workspaces/{id}/ cross-workspace guard (middleware.go:143-160) blocks spoofing the workspace segment, with documented exemptions for platform admins and the 'current' keyword.

A source-level regression guard (gallery_authorization_source_test.go) statically asserts gallery and album object handlers route through requireGalleryInWorkspace/requireAlbumInWorkspace, preventing future regressions on those two handlers.

AssetRepo.BulkMoveToGallery (asset_repo.go:584) and the bulk mutation helpers (BulkUpdateStatus/BulkSetRating/BulkSetColorLabel/BulkAddTags/BulkRemoveTags) all carry an explicit `workspace_id = $N` predicate, and BulkMoveToGallery additionally verifies both galleries belong to the workspace — correct application-layer scoping for the bulk path.
AssetRepo.GetByIDAndWorkspace (asset_repo.go:425) exists as the correct workspace-scoped single-asset lookup primitive (it is simply not used by the asset GET/download/delete handlers).

seamFlows.seam: S3: gallery/album → uploader authorization & asset linkage
seamFlows.flowDescription:
An upload is NOT bound to a gallery at the backend at all — gallery linkage is a separate, client-orchestrated second step. Trace:

1. CreateSession (backend/internal/handler/chunked_upload.go:288) reads workspace_id and user_id from context (getWorkspaceID → middleware.WorkspaceIDFromContext; getUserID → middleware.JWTClaimsFromContext). The JSON body it decodes (lines 296-302) is ONLY {filename, content_type, total_size, chunk_size, scan_manifest} — there is NO gallery_id or album_id field anywhere. The upload session row (repository.UploadSession built at lines 477-489) carries WorkspaceID + UserID but no gallery target. The frontend confirms this: frontend/src/hooks/use-upload.ts:101-107 POSTs exactly those five fields, never a gallery id.

2. CreateSession reserves storage quota (storageAccountingSvc.ReserveUpload, line 354), reserves an upload credit (creditGate.ReserveForSession, line 402), then initiates an S3/B2 multipart upload (CreateMultipartUpload, line 460) under key "<workspaceID>/<tusUploadID>/original<ext>" (line 448). Both reservations are workspace-scoped, not gallery-scoped.

3. UploadChunk (chunked_upload.go:527) streams parts to B2, and when offset >= total_size calls finalizeUpload (line 722).

4. finalizeUpload (chunked_upload.go:859) composes the object, verifies the F-003 hash + header/trailer bytes, then inserts the asset row (lines 949-973) via assetRepo.Create. The asset gets WorkspaceID = session.WorkspaceID and Status = "processing" — but it is NEVER inserted into gallery_assets. It commits the storage reservation (CommitUploadReservation, line 979) and consumes the credit (line 767). The response returns the asset id (line 996-1002).

5. WebP/EXIF: finalize sets Status="processing" only. The async ThumbnailWorker (backend/internal/worker/thumbnail_worker.go:176 processNextBatch → ListByStatus("processing")) polls every 1s, downloads the original, runs thumbnailSvc.GenerateAll (cwebp derivatives), persists asset_derivatives + thumbnail_urls, runs exifSvc.ExtractAndStore, sets Status="ready", and emits asset.ready. So derivatives/EXIF are triggered indirectly via status, not synchronously on finalize.

6. Gallery linkage happens entirely client-side AFTER upload: frontend/src/app/(dashboard)/galleries/[id]/page.tsx:769-831 has a useEffect that, for each completed upload item, calls addAssetToGallery(token, galleryId, assetId, 0) → POST /api/v1/galleries/{id}/assets, then optionally addAlbumAssets → POST /api/v1/albums/{id}/assets.

7. AddAsset (backend/internal/handler/gallery_handler.go:621) validates the GALLERY belongs to the caller's workspace via requireGalleryInWorkspace (line 628) but does NOT validate the supplied asset_id belongs to that workspace. gallerySvc.AddAsset (backend/internal/service/gallery_service.go:200) is a passthrough to galleryAssetRepo.Add (backend/internal/repository/gallery_asset_repo.go:33) which is a bare INSERT into gallery_assets. The migration (013_create_gallery_assets.up.sql) has FKs to galleries(id) and assets(id) individually but NO cross-table workspace consistency check. Album AddAssets (album_handler.go:213) and AlbumService.AddAsset (album_service.go:144) have the identical unguarded-asset pattern.

8. Read side does not compensate: ListAssets (gallery_handler.go:788) returns raw gallery_assets junction rows; the frontend hydrates each via GET /api/v1/assets/{id} → AssetHandler.GetByID (asset_handler.go:66) → AssetService.GetByID (asset_service.go:38) → assetRepo.GetByID(id) which is NOT workspace-scoped.
workingWell: Workspace context is correctly resolved at CreateSession: getWorkspaceID reads middleware.WorkspaceIDFromContext and rejects missing/pending workspaces (chunked_upload.go:289-293), and the routes are mounted under JWTAuth + TenantContext (cmd/api/main.go:1557-1648), so the uploader's own workspace is trustworthy and used for the asset's WorkspaceID and the storage key.

Storage-quota reservation is race-safe and correctly settled: ReserveUpload uses an atomic conditional UPDATE that fails closed on quota (storage_accounting_service.go:190-233), CreateSession reserves before the B2 multipart call and releases on every early-exit path (chunked_upload.go:370-377, 412, 430, 456, 462, 504), finalize converts reserve→used via CommitUploadReservation (line 979), and Cancel/expiry release it (line 831, finalizeUpload releaseReservation closures).

Upload-credit metering is correctly wired across the lifecycle: reserve at CreateSession (line 402), consume on success (line 767), and refund on every failure class — hash mismatch, manifest invalid/required, infra failure, and user cancel (lines 731-759, 844) — with refund failures logged for reconciliation (logRefundFailure).

WebP-derivative + EXIF generation IS reliably triggered: finalize sets Status='processing' (chunked_upload.go:957) and the ThumbnailWorker polls that status on a 1s loop, generates all cwebp variants, persists asset_derivatives + thumbnail_urls, extracts EXIF, then flips to 'ready' and emits asset.ready (thumbnail_worker.go:176-318). The gallery grid shows the tile immediately and the frontend SSE+4s-poll fallback refreshes it when ready (galleries/[id]/page.tsx:711-747).

Orphaned-object cleanup on the upload side is solid: the asset-insert-failure path deletes the assembled B2 object (persistAssetOrCleanup, chunked_upload.go:1018; F-005 regression test chunked_upload_orphan_test.go), the hash/manifest/digest failure paths delete it (lines 927-944), and the UploadSessionCleanupWorker aborts abandoned multipart uploads + deletes expired, non-completed sessions (upload_session_cleanup_worker.go; ListExpired filters completed_at IS NULL).

The gallery-side authorization helper itself is correct and enforced by a guard test: requireGalleryInWorkspace verifies gallery.WorkspaceID == caller workspace (gallery_handler.go:115-131) and gallery_authorization_source_test.go asserts every gallery-scoped route calls it.

BulkMoveToGallery is the correct reference implementation for cross-tenant safety: it validates BOTH galleries and the asset set belong to the workspace inside a transaction (asset_repo.go:584-670), showing the codebase knows the right pattern — it is just not applied at the AddAsset/AddAssets linkage seam.

seamFlows.seam: S4: gallery → viewer/client delivery (public access, share, proofing, download)
seamFlows.flowDescription: There are TWO distinct viewer systems and the seam blurs them. (A) Live-streaming viewer: `/api/v1/public/streams/...` and `/api/v1/public/s/{code}` mounted via streaming/handlers/routes.go RegisterPublicRoutes (no transport JWT), authed inside each handler with the streaming/viewer.Service JWT (HS256, audience `viewer-access`, dedicated KEK-encrypted key from platform_settings). middleware/viewer_context.go (ViewerContext / RequireViewerSession / ViewerSessionFromContext) is the viewer-JWT extractor for the stream chat/SSE RLS path. (B) Gallery client delivery: the actual photographer-client surface lives under `/api/v1/public/galleries/{slug}/...` registered by RegisterPublicGalleryRoutes (routes_m2.go:371, mounted on the outer no-auth router `r` at main.go:1651) and does NOT use the viewer JWT at all — it uses gallery `password_hash` + an in-memory `gallery_session` token (GalleryAccessService.VerifyPassword → ValidateSession). \n\nGallery read flow: PublicGalleryPage (app/g/[slug]/page.tsx) calls getPublicGallery → GET /galleries/{slug} (GetBySlug, public_gallery_handler.go:231) which checks IsPublished + ExpiresAt only, and exposes `settings.has_password`. The Next page shows GalleryPasswordGate when has_password && no `gallery_session` cookie. Listing endpoints (ListAssets:380, ListAlbums:452, ListAlbumAssets:498, PublicAssetDownload:1238) DO call requirePublicGallerySession (public_gallery_handler.go:154) which validates the gallery_session token via accessSvc.ValidateSession. Images themselves render via getStorageBackedUrl (frontend lib/dashboard-ui.ts:90) → `${API_BASE}/storage/<storage_key>`; the storage proxy (main.go:2498) serves `thumbnails/<uuid>/<variant>.webp` keys ANONYMOUSLY (isPublicThumbnailKey, main.go:352, regex main.go:325) and requires an RS256 platform JWT + storageKeyBelongsToWorkspace for everything else. display_webp full-res lives under derivatives/ (auth-required) so the lightbox prefers thumb_lg_webp (public). Downloads go through PublicAssetDownload which verifies asset-in-gallery, DownloadEnabled, expiry, password session, and format/watermark choice. Proofing submit (proofingHandler.SubmitPublic, proofing_handler.go:117) is public-by-slug and gates on the same gallery_session. Share links (ShareLinkService) are a parallel, largely-disconnected system: /share/{token}/verify validates PIN/expiry/access-count but issues no session and no downstream endpoint consults it.
workingWell: Streaming viewer JWT audience isolation holds: streaming/viewer/jwt.go Parse pins HS256 (WithValidMethods + method check line 169), requires exp, validates issuer + audience `viewer-access` (lines 162-167), and rejects refresh-audience tokens used as access tokens. The platform ParseAccessToken (auth.go:362-372) requires RS256 (*jwt.SigningMethodRSA) + jwt.WithAudience(jwtAudience) with a different (RSA) key, so a viewer HS256 token can never authenticate platform/owner endpoints, and vice-versa.

Cross-stream isolation is enforced: both chat_viewer_handler.go:103 and viewer_public_handler.go:113 reject when claims.StreamID != path {streamID/id}, collapsing mismatch to 404 (anti-enumeration). Stream chat/reactions/SSE mount on the public router but auth inside the handler via the viewer service, never the workspace JWT.

Cross-gallery isolation on the face/people surface is correctly gallery-scoped: FaceMatch uses FindSimilarFacesInGallery (public_gallery_handler.go:868), ListPersonPhotos and PhotoSearch use ListClusterAssetIDsInGallery / FindSimilarFacesInGalleryScored (lines 1023, 1142, 1209), so a guest of gallery A cannot enumerate identities/photos from gallery B in the same workspace.

Workspace-subdomain scoping is strict: resolveGalleryForRequest (public_gallery_handler.go:218) does NOT fall back to unscoped lookup on a `?ws=` miss, closing the documented 2026-05-28 cross-workspace slug-resolution hole.
Album cross-gallery check: ListAlbumAssets verifies album.GalleryID == gallery.ID (public_gallery_handler.go:521) before listing, so an album id from another gallery returns 404.

Gallery password IS enforced server-side (not UI-only) on the JSON listing + download endpoints via requirePublicGallerySession, and the gallery_session cookie is HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict (gallery_access_handler.go:65-73).

PublicAssetDownload enforces asset-in-gallery membership, DownloadEnabled, expiry, and password session before streaming, and the download format selector (publicDownloadVariant, public_gallery_handler.go:1362) only ever maps to the asset's own original/webp/thumbnail keys.
The /storage/* proxy streams bytes through the API (never leaks the B2/S3 host) and sanitizes keys before the auth decision (validateStorageKey, main.go:332; F-035).

seamFlows.flowDescription: Platform JWTs are RS256, minted by jwtService.GenerateAccessToken (backend/internal/auth/auth.go:337-360) with claims sub/workspace_id/role/platform_role/state_id/mfa_verified plus iss+aud=rawdrive-api. ParseAccessToken (auth.go:362-408) enforces issuer+audience binding. middleware.JWTAuth (jwt_auth.go:11-54) parses the bearer token and copies exactly seven keys into a claimsMap (sub, user_id, workspace_id, role, platform_role, state_id, mfa_verified) which it stashes via WithJWTClaims. Every authenticated handler / role middleware reads it back via JWTClaimsFromContext (middleware.go:40-45). TenantContext (middleware.go:109-190) pulls workspace_id+state_id from claims, enforces a cross-workspace URL guard for any path containing /workspaces/ (with explicit exemptions for platform admins on /api/v1/admin/* and the literal "current" segment), and sets RLS context. The protected data-plane group (cmd/api/main.go:1557-1568) chains JWTAuth -> TenantContext -> PlanTierContext -> optional RequireMFA. RequireState (middleware.go:285-307) only checks state_id is non-empty and is mounted on the legacy /workspace + /team group (main.go:1269-1280). Login (handler.go:425-519) and OAuthGoogleCallback (handler.go:697-794) both route the MFA step-up decision through the single shared requiresMFAStepUp predicate (handler.go:682-695); on a verified+active enrollment both mint a short-lived RS256 mfa_challenge token (purpose=mfa_challenge, no iss/aud, parsed by parseChallengeRaw which requires purpose match) and withhold full tokens. VerifyTOTP / VerifyRecoveryCode (mfa_handler.go) then mint access+refresh with mfa_verified=true and a fresh per-session family UUID via GenerateRefreshTokenWithMFA. RotateRefreshToken (auth.go:497-589) carries Sub/WorkspaceID/Role/PlatformRole/StateID/MFAVerified from the stored RefreshSessionEntry forward into both the new refresh row and the new access token; the RefreshToken handler (handler.go:796-845) additionally re-resolves workspace claims from DB to upgrade a post-onboarding access token, preserving MFAVerified. The viewer JWT (streaming/viewer/jwt.go) is a fully separate HS256 primitive with its own platform_settings signing key and audiences viewer-access/viewer-refresh, parsed only by middleware.ViewerContext on /api/v1/public/streams/* — no overlap with the platform RS256 key. API-key auth (api_key_auth.go) is a third path that sets workspace_id context keys but NOT the JWT claims map.
workingWell: Login and OAuthGoogleCallback share the single requiresMFAStepUp predicate (handler.go:682-695), and the F-012 regression test (oauth_mfa_stepup_test.go) asserts the OAuth gate runs BEFORE any full-session refresh token is issued — OAuth cannot bypass TOTP step-up.

RotateRefreshToken preserves mfa_verified, workspace_id, role, platform_role, state_id from the persisted RefreshSessionEntry into both the rotated refresh row and the new access token (auth.go:541-582); the RefreshSessionRepo persists and re-reads all of these columns (refresh_session_repo.go:42-72). A refresh never silently downgrades mfa_verified.
The RefreshToken handler re-resolves workspace claims from DB and explicitly carries MFAVerified forward when regenerating the access token post-onboarding (handler.go:826-833).

MFA challenge tokens carry purpose=mfa_challenge and parseChallengeRaw rejects any token lacking that purpose (mfa_handler.go:836-839), so a normal access token cannot be replayed as a challenge and vice-versa. Challenge tokens are single-use via the consumedChallenges denylist (mfa_handler.go:446-449, 747-779).

Viewer JWTs are cryptographically isolated from platform JWTs: different algorithm (HS256 vs RS256), different signing key (platform_settings streaming.viewer_jwt_signing_key vs the RS256 keypair), and distinct audiences enforced via jwt.WithAudience(viewerAccessAudience) (viewer/jwt.go:161-167). The platform ParseAccessToken enforces aud=rawdrive-api (auth.go:371-372). Neither can validate the other's tokens.
GenerateAccessToken rejects tokens missing sub/workspace_id/role/state_id (auth.go:338), so a malformed onboarding token cannot be minted.

TenantContext enforces a cross-workspace URL guard for /workspaces/{id} paths with deliberate, documented exemptions (platform admins on /api/v1/admin/*, the literal 'current' segment) — handlers like StorageConfigHandler.TestConnection and WebhookHandler that read {workspaceId} from the URL are transitively protected because their routes sit under /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/... (routes_m2.go:241,357).

confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: Account-takeover / pre-hijack: an attacker registers a password account with victim@gmail.com (supplying any phone), never verifies it. Later the victim signs in with Google; HandleGoogleCallback finds the attacker's row by email and logs the victim straight into the attacker-controlled account (which still has the attacker's known password). Symmetrically, a Google account whose email is unverified-at-Google could assert an arbitrary email and link to/log in as a matching RawDrive account, because email_verified is never demanded from Google either. This is the classic OAuth 'unverified email' takeover.
confirmedGaps.recommendation: 1) Add `EmailVerified bool `json:"email_verified"`` to the Google userinfo payload struct and reject the callback when it is false. 2) Before linking to an existing row in HandleGoogleCallback, refuse to auto-link/log in to an account whose stored email_verified is FALSE (or require completing the email-OTP flow first). confirmedGaps.refuteReasoning: I read the full OAuth callback path and found no email_verified gate on either side. Prong A (pre-registration hijack): Register persists a users row with email_verified=FALSE (handler.go:383 -> user/repo.go:46-49; migration 006_add_password_to_users.up.sql:5 sets DEFAULT FALSE), and I found NO cleanup/pruning of unverified rows anywhere in migrations or the user/auth packages. HandleGoogleCallback then does FindByEmail(profile.Email) (auth.go:722) and, if a row exists, immediately LinkOAuth + returns the existing user as authenticated (auth.go:727-744) with zero verification check. The auth.User struct (auth.go:40-45) does not even carry an EmailVerified field, and the concrete oauthUserStore.FindByEmail (cmd/api/oauth_store.go:25-40) maps only ID/Email/DisplayName/AvatarURL — so the callback structurally CANNOT inspect verification state even if it wanted to. The HTTP handler OAuthGoogleCallback then mints a refresh token and redirects authenticated=1 (handler.go:779-792), so the linker is fully logged into the pre-existing (attacker-controlled) account. The users.email UNIQUE constraint (002_create_users.up.sql:3) actually strengthens the attack: once the attacker pre-registers victim@gmail.com, the victim's only remaining path is Sign-in-with-Google (re-registration returns 409 at handler.go:378), which lands them in the attacker's row. Prong B (unverified-at-Google): GetProfile decodes only sub/email/name/picture (google_provider.go:94-99) and never reads or asserts the OIDC email_verified claim — grep confirms the strings email_verified/EmailVerified appear NOWHERE in google_provider.go, OAuthProfile, or the oauth tests. I could not find any compensating control (no MFA gate helps here since the attacker's pre-created account has no enrollment; the requiresMFAStepUp branch at handler.go:755 only fires if the TARGET account enrolled TOTP, which a freshly-planted attacker row will not have). This is the classic OAuth unverified-email account takeover; both prongs are real and unmitigated. CRITICAL stands — it is a cross-account authentication bypass on the platform-user JWT audience.

confirmedGaps.title: Image bytes (thumbnails) served fully anonymously — bypasses gallery password, expiry, publish state, and access-mode
confirmedGaps.location: backend/cmd/api/main.go:2498-2549 (isPublicThumbnailKey bypass) + main.go:352 + regex main.go:325
confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: Anyone who learns/guesses an asset UUID (e.g. from a leaked JSON response, a referrer, or by enumerating the listing of a since-password-protected gallery) can fetch the full visible image bytes of a password-protected, unpublished, or expired gallery directly via /storage/thumbnails/<uuid>/thumb_lg_webp.webp. The password/expiry gate protects only the metadata listing, not the photos themselves — defeating the entire client-privacy guarantee of gallery passwords and expiry.
confirmedGaps.recommendation: Do not serve gallery image bytes purely on key shape. Either (a) require the gallery_session token (or a signed, gallery+asset+expiry-scoped URL token) on the thumbnail path and verify the asset belongs to a published, non-expired, password-satisfied gallery, or (b) issue short-lived signed image URLs per authorized session. At minimum, gate isPublicThumbnail bytes behind the same gallery-state checks the JSON listing uses.
confirmedGaps.refuteReasoning: Verified the full chain end-to-end. (1) The /storage/* proxy is registered on the base router r (main.go:2498), which carries only CORS/Logger/Recoverer/RequestID/SecurityHeaders/RateLimit (main.go:810-832) — no auth middleware. (2) main.go:2520 computes isPublicThumbnail=isPublicThumbnailKey(key); when true, the entire token-parse + storageKeyBelongsToWorkspace block (2522-2549) is skipped and execution falls straight to storageProvider.Get(key) at 2551. No gallery lookup, password, publish, expiry, or workspace check on the byte path. (3) publicThumbnailKeyRe (main.go:325) matches thumbnails/<uuid>/(thumb_sm|thumb_md|thumb_lg|display).webp, and webpStorageKey (thumbnail_service.go:331-336) writes thumb_sm/md/lg_webp exactly under thumbnails/<asset>/<name>.webp — so these are the very bytes the grid (public-gallery-grid.tsx:701-712) and lightbox (1053-1061) render. getStorageBackedUrl (dashboard-ui.ts:90-114) emits a bare /storage/<key> URL with NO token for public viewers (token arg omitted). (4) The password/publish/expiry gates live ONLY on the JSON listing handlers: requirePublicGallerySession (public_gallery_handler.go:154-169), IsPublished (247-250, 383-389), expiry (253-260). They do not protect bytes. (5) The asset UUID — the join key — is exposed: publicAssetResponse.ID = asset.ID.String() (public_gallery_handler.go:419) and the raw thumbnail_urls map values contain the UUID. Consequence: anyone who obtains an asset UUID (gallery that was public/indexed before a password/expiry was applied, a leaked/forwarded listing, a referer) can fetch thumb_lg_webp (~1200px) and display.webp anonymously forever — the proxy intentionally emits stable, non-expiring URLs (main.go:2493). I did NOT find any compensating control: no HMAC/signed-URL on thumbnail keys (the only sign references are JWT/webhook signatures), no per-gallery scoping in the regex, no later gate. The bypass is deliberate and documented (main.go:2511-2519; thumbnail_service.go:314-325), but the documented justification ('the exact bytes a visitor already receives') only holds for a currently-accessible gallery and silently fails for password-protected/expired/unpublished ones. One honest mitigant: asset IDs are UUIDv4 (122 random bits) so blind enumeration is infeasible — an attacker must obtain a UUID rather than brute-force it. That bounds mass-scraping but does not restore the password/expiry privacy guarantee for any known/leaked UUID. Severity stays CRITICAL: it is a client-privacy / tenant-isolation hole on the actual image bytes, defeating the core purpose of gallery passwords and expiry.

confirmedGaps.title: Share-link PIN / expiry / access-count enforcement is advisory only — never gates asset delivery
confirmedGaps.location: backend/internal/handler/share_link_handler.go:256-294 (Verify) + routes_m2.go:463-466 + public_gallery_handler.go:154
confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: A client given an expired share link, a PIN-locked share link, or a link that has hit its max_access_count can ignore the verify step entirely and load the gallery + all photos by hitting /api/v1/public/galleries/{slug}/assets and /storage/thumbnails/... directly. (1) ShareLinkHandler.Verify (share_link_handler.go:256-294) runs ValidateAccess + TrackAccess then returns 200 {"status":"ok"} and sets NO cookie/session (lines 292-293) — the result is purely advisory to a cooperating client. (2) The ONLY gate on the public delivery endpoints (ListAssets, ListAlbumAssets, PublicAssetDownload) is requirePublicGallerySession (public_gallery_handler.go:154-169), which consults exclusively gallery.PasswordHash + the gallery_session cookie/X-Gallery-Session header via accessSvc.ValidateSession; it never references the share link, its PIN, expiry, or access count, and returns true unconditionally when the gallery has no PasswordHash (lines 155-156). (4) Frontend /g/[slug]/page.tsx reads only the gallery_session cookie (line 61) and forwards it as X-Gallery-Session (galleries.ts:600,620) — it never reads ?share= and never calls the verify endpoint. (5) The GAL-FR-112 client helper verifyShareLink (galleries.ts:211) has ZERO callers in the entire frontend (grep returned only its own definition); its comment admits it is "wired on a per-deployment basis," i.e. not in the standard flow. (6) /storage/thumbnails/<uuid>/<variant>.webp (main.go:2498-2520) is served fully anonymously by design (isPublicThumbnail bypass) with no JWT, no gallery-password, and no share-token check. Net result: a client given an expired / PIN-locked / access-capped share link can bypass Verify entirely and hit GET /api/v1/public/galleries/{slug}/assets, .../download, and /storage/thumbnails/... directly. Share-link expiry/PIN/access caps provide no real protection — they are enforceable only by a cooperating client. The only caveat is that a SEPARATE mechanism, the gallery-level password (SetPassword -> gallery.PasswordHash), still gates /assets and /download (but NOT thumbnails) when a gallery password is set; that is independent of share links and does not rescue galleries whose access posture relies on the share-link controls. Severity CRITICAL stands: a documented access-control feature (expiry/PIN/access-cap on share links) silently fails open at the asset-delivery layer. confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: Workspace A can overwrite the cover photo/style/template, design config, and embedded videos of any workspace B gallery (defacement / brand sabotage), and read B's design config. UpdateCover can even point cover_asset_id at an arbitrary asset UUID with no membership check.
confirmedGaps.recommendation: Compare gallery.WorkspaceID against ctx workspace in UpdateCover; add a workspace check (or scope the design service) in all three GalleryDesignHandler methods; validate cover asset_id belongs to the same workspace.
confirmedGaps.refuteReasoning:
The gap is real at every layer I checked, and the DB-layer RLS that could have saved it is not enforced in production.

Handler layer (no scoping):
- gallery_cover_handler.go:116 calls h.galleryRepo.GetByID(ctx, galleryID) with only the URL id, then at :147 calls h.galleryRepo.Update(ctx, gallery). It never reads the caller's workspace from context and never compares gallery.WorkspaceID. UpdateCover also sets gallery.CoverAssetID from an arbitrary asset UUID (:135-137) with no membership check on the asset.
- gallery_design_handler.go:24-141: GetDesign/UpdateDesign/UpdateEmbeddedVideos pass the URL id straight to designSvc with no workspace param.

Service layer (no scoping): gallery_design_service.go:126/179/237 — GetDesignConfig, UpdateDesignConfigRaw, UpdateEmbeddedVideos each take only galleryID, fetch via the unscoped GetByID, mutate gallery.Settings, and call galleryRepo.Update.

Repo layer (no scoping): gallery_repo.go:205-230 GetByID is WHERE id=$1 AND deleted_at IS NULL (no workspace_id); :344-369 Update is WHERE id=$29 AND deleted_at IS NULL (no workspace_id). So the repo cannot enforce tenancy; the caller must.

The established contract proves these are outliers: the sibling GalleryHandler.GetByID/Update/SoftDelete all go through requireGalleryInWorkspace (gallery_handler.go:115-131), which fetches then rejects with 404 when gallery.WorkspaceID != workspaceID. The cover/design handlers simply omit this check.

I checked the two plausible "handled elsewhere" defenses and both fail:
1. Per-route ownership middleware: routes_m2.go:85-200 mounts these on the /api/v1/galleries group whose only middleware (main.go:1557-1568) is JWTAuth + TenantContext + PlanTierContext. TenantContext (middleware.go:109-164) only does a same-workspace URL check for paths containing /workspaces/ (:143) — gallery paths are /api/v1/galleries/{id}/... and never hit that branch; {id} is a gallery UUID, never validated against the caller's workspace.
2. Postgres RLS: galleries DOES have a USING policy (008_create_rls.up.sql:44-48) keyed on app.workspace_id, set per-request by TenantContext via PgDBContext.SetWorkspaceID (db_context.go:29-37). BUT: (a) test_helpers.go:19-20 explicitly states the DB user is a superuser that bypasses RLS, and the RLS-respecting rawdrive_app role is only entered via SET ROLE in test helpers; (b) the production pool (main.go:840-851) is built with pgxpool.NewWithConfig and has no AfterConnect/SET ROLE rawdrive_app anywhere (grep for AfterConnect/SET ROLE/bypass_rls in non-test code returned zero matches); (c) no migration uses FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (grep returned nothing), so the table-owner/superuser connection bypasses RLS entirely; (d) compose runs Postgres as POSTGRES_USER=${PROJECT_USER} (the owner). Additionally SetWorkspaceID uses set_config(..., is_local=false) on a pooled connection that is released before the repo's separate pool checkout runs the query — an unreliable carry-over even if RLS were enforced. Net: RLS does not protect these endpoints in production.

Therefore Workspace A, authenticated with its own valid JWT, can PUT /galleries/{B's id}/cover, /design, and /embedded-videos to deface workspace B's galleries, and GET /design to read B's design config. Confirmed cross-tenant write+read.

Severity HIGH (not CRITICAL): it requires a valid authenticated photographer account and an enumerated/known target gallery UUID, and the damage is gallery branding/cover/design/embedded-video defacement plus design-config read — brand sabotage and an isolation hole, but not direct exfiltration of client photos or platform-wide takeover. Matches the claimed HIGH.

confirmedGaps.title: Edge derivative delivery serves any asset's WebP by UUID with no gallery/workspace check
confirmedGaps.location: backend/internal/handler/edge_delivery_handler.go:24-121 (ServeDerivative parses assetId from URL, fetches storage_key from asset_derivatives or guesses the path, streams the derivative); mounted authenticated at backend/internal/handler/routes_m3.go:53 (/api/v1/edge/{assetId}/{variant}) with no ownership filter
confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: Any authenticated user can fetch any asset's display_webp (2400px) or thumbnails from any workspace by enumerating asset UUIDs — a cross-tenant image-content leak that also bypasses gallery publish/password/expiry gates.
confirmedGaps.recommendation: Resolve the asset's workspace_id (AssetRepo already returns it) and require it to equal the caller's workspace, or require a valid gallery membership + gallery access gate before streaming.
confirmedGaps.refuteReasoning: The edge handler ServeDerivative (edge_delivery_handler.go:24-121) parses an arbitrary assetId, resolves storage_key, calls the UNSCOPED assetRepo.GetByID (asset_repo.go:116, query `WHERE id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL` — no workspace filter), and streams the derivative. It never reads the caller's workspace from JWT/tenant context and never compares asset.WorkspaceID to the caller. The route is mounted inside the api group (main.go:1557-1568) which applies JWTAuth + TenantContext, so a VALID platform JWT is required — but TenantContext's only ownership guard (middleware.go:143-161) fires only for URLs containing `/workspaces/`; the edge path `/api/v1/edge/{assetId}/{variant}` has no such segment, so no app-layer ownership check runs. I checked the only plausible mitigation, RLS: migration 061 (061_rls_extension_f009.up.sql:50,104-108) enables assets_isolation keyed on current_setting('app.workspace_id'), set by TenantContext via PgDBContext.SetWorkspaceID (db_context.go:29-37). This mitigation is INEFFECTIVE at runtime for two independent reasons. (1) Owner bypass: the app connects as the table-owning `rawdrive` Postgres role (docker-compose.dev.yml:80; deploy/.env.example:30 DATABASE_URL), not the non-login rawdrive_app role the RLS migration targeted (008_create_rls.up.sql:1-6); Postgres exempts table owners from RLS unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set, and grep found NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY anywhere in migrations. (2) Connection/session mismatch: SetWorkspaceID runs set_config(..., is_local=false) via a one-shot pool.Exec and returns the conn to the 25-conn pgxpool with no AfterAcquire hook, transaction, or per-request pinning, so the handler's assetRepo.Pool().QueryRow may run on a different connection lacking app.workspace_id. Net: any authenticated platform user can enumerate asset UUIDs to pull any workspace's display_webp/thumbnails, bypassing gallery publish/password/expiry gates (the handler never consults galleries). The same RLS-dependence affects AssetService.GetByID (asset_service.go:38-39) broadly, but the edge handler is a concrete directly-exploitable instance. Severity HIGH (not CRITICAL) because a valid platform JWT is required — it is an authenticated cross-tenant content leak, a genuine tenant-isolation hole.

confirmedGaps.title: Public asset listing/download enforce only gallery password — share-link PIN/expiry/access-count and gallery access_mode are never enforced
confirmedGaps.location: backend/internal/handler/public_gallery_handler.go:154-169 requirePublicGallerySession checks ONLY gallery.PasswordHash; ListAssets/ListAlbums/ListAlbumAssets/PublicAssetDownload (:380-559, :1238-1352) gate on IsPublished + that password session; access_mode (migration 041:102 default 'private') is never read on any public path; share_link_service.ValidateAccess (:170-228) enforces PIN/expiry/max_access_count but is only invoked by the standalone /public/share/{token}/verify endpoint which sets no session and gates nothing downstream
confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: A published gallery with access_mode='private'/'invite-only', or protected only by a PIN/expiring/access-capped share link (and no gallery-level password), is fully readable and downloadable by anyone who has the slug — the share-link controls and access_mode are decorative. Expired or access-exhausted share links still serve assets.
confirmedGaps.recommendation: Make the asset/album/download endpoints require and validate the share token (ValidateAccess + TrackAccess) when the gallery is reached via a share link, and enforce access_mode on the public read path; bind a verified share-token to the gallery_session so downstream endpoints actually require it.
confirmedGaps.refuteReasoning:
Read every cited path and surrounding code; the gap is real and nothing elsewhere closes it.

(1) PIN/expiry/access-count are decorative on the read/download path. requirePublicGallerySession (public_gallery_handler.go:155-168) returns true unless gallery.PasswordHash is non-empty, and otherwise only consults accessSvc.ValidateSession. ListAssets (:383-389), ListAlbums (:459-466), ListAlbumAssets (:511-518) and PublicAssetDownload (:1257-1263) gate solely on IsPublished + requirePublicGallerySession (download additionally checks ExpiresAt and DownloadEnabled). ShareLinkService.ValidateAccess (share_link_service.go:177-227) does enforce revocation, expiry, MaxAccessCount, and PIN/password/email modes — but it is invoked ONLY by ShareLinkHandler.Verify (share_link_handler.go:256-294). That handler returns {"status":"ok"} and mints NO session token / sets NO cookie. The gallery session map (gallery_access_service.go:78) is written ONLY by VerifyPassword, so a successful share-link verify produces nothing the read handlers consume. A gallery with no gallery-level password protected only by a PIN/expiring/access-capped share link is therefore fully readable/downloadable by slug alone, and expired or access-exhausted links keep serving.

(2) access_mode is unenforceable, not merely unread. Migration 041:102 adds access_mode NOT NULL DEFAULT 'private' with a CHECK for invite-only/private/unlisted/public. But the repository.Gallery struct (gallery_repo.go:15-...) has NO AccessMode field — every SELECT scan list (e.g. :217, :245, :325) omits it, and the only reference is the UpdateField column allowlist at :508. So access_mode is a write-only column; no public handler or middleware can read it (confirmed: no access_mode reference anywhere under internal/middleware/). Default 'private'/'invite-only' galleries that are published are served to anyone with the slug.

Severity nuance: part (1) is HIGH (PIN/expiry/access-count controls a photographer explicitly configured are silently bypassed). Part (2) is arguably MEDIUM in isolation because publishing a gallery is the operative gate and the slug carries an 8-char UUID suffix (resolveGalleryForRequest :211), so it is unlisted-by-obscurity rather than openly enumerable. But access_mode='invite-only' on a published gallery conveying an authorization intent that is wholly ignored, combined with the share-link bypass, keeps the aggregate finding at HIGH. Not CRITICAL: workspace/tenant isolation itself holds (resolveGalleryForRequest strictly scopes ?ws= lookups, :219-224), and an unpublished gallery still 404s, so this is a missing per-gallery access-control layer, not a tenant-isolation hole.

confirmedGaps.title: Production DB connects as table-owner role, silently bypassing all RLS tenant-isolation policies
confirmedGaps.location: backend/cmd/api/main.go:835-851; .env.cobolt:12; backend/internal/database/migrations/061_rls_extension_f009.up.sql
confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: Every RLS policy is inert in production. The DB provides ZERO tenant isolation; isolation depends entirely on application-layer workspace_id predicates. Any handler/repo path that omits a workspace check (see S2-G2..G6) reads or mutates other workspaces' data with no DB backstop. This converts each missing application check from defence-in-depth lapse into a live cross-tenant data breach.
confirmedGaps.recommendation: Connect the API as a dedicated non-owner role that does not bypass RLS (create `rawdrive_app` with LOGIN, point DATABASE_URL at it), OR add `ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` for every tenant-scoped table so even the owner is subject to policy. Additionally, set app.workspace_id on the actual query connection (e.g. pgxpool AfterConnect that runs per-acquire, or wrap each request's queries in a transaction that runs SET LOCAL) since the current pool.Exec(set_config,...) does not reliably bind to the connection later repos use.
confirmedGaps.refuteReasoning: The claim is factually correct on every cited point. (1) Production connects as the table-owner role: main.go:840-851 builds the pgxpool straight from DATABASE_URL with no role hook; .env.cobolt:12 and deploy/.env.example:7,30 both use user `rawdrive` (= POSTGRES_USER, the DB/table owner). Postgres does not enforce RLS against a table owner unless FORCE is set. (2) No FORCE on the protected tables: migrations 008 and 061 only ENABLE RLS. Grep across all migration SQL shows FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY appears ONLY in the F-014 streaming migrations (082:47,79 on chat_messages/reaction_events; also 084-088) — proving the team knew about FORCE and applied it to streaming tables but NOT to galleries/assets/api_keys/subscriptions/workspace_storage/etc. Those 008+061 policies are therefore inert against the owner role. (3) No SET ROLE in production: `SET ROLE rawdrive_app` appears only in test_helpers.go (82/113/153/166/205) and chat_repo_rls_test.go:143; rawdrive_app is created NOLOGIN (008:6) so it cannot be connected to directly and the app never assumes it; poolCfg only sets MaxConns/MinConns (main.go:844-845), no AfterConnect/BeforeAcquire. I could not find any code path that rescues this. A prior internal audit independently reached the same conclusion (docs/audits/gallery-360-audit-2026-05-30.md:415,550). I also found a deeper, related flaw: db_context.go:30-31 sets app.workspace_id with is_local=false on a pooled connection via pool.Exec, while handler queries run on possibly different pooled connections (25-conn pool), so even on the FORCE'd streaming tables the GUC and the query can desynchronize. The intentional-design notes (viewer JWT audience, etc.) do not apply — RLS is a DB-layer tenant backstop and it is genuinely non-functional in prod. I downgrade from CRITICAL to HIGH only because RLS here is defense-in-depth: real tenant isolation depends on application-layer workspace_id predicates, and the prior audit made the same Critical->High adjustment (gallery-360-audit:469). It escalates to CRITICAL only when combined with a separately-confirmed missing application-layer check.

The junction row is created; the asset then surfaces in A's gallery listing. Combined with S3-G3 (unscoped GET /assets/{id}) this yields full cross-tenant photo exfiltration: link victim's asset → list gallery → fetch the asset's storage-backed download URL. AddAsset (gallery_handler.go:622-653) calls requireGalleryInWorkspace (defined at gallery_handler.go:115-131), which only loads the gallery via GetByID and asserts gallery.WorkspaceID == workspaceID — it validates the GALLERY's tenancy, nothing about the asset. The route (routes_m2.go:94) sits in the standard JWT-protected /api/v1/galleries block with no per-asset middleware. I confirmed the codebase author KNOWS this guard is needed: BulkMoveToGallery (asset_repo.go:584-670) explicitly filters assetIDs by `WHERE id = ANY($1) AND workspace_id = $2 AND deleted_at IS NULL` and silently drops cross-workspace IDs, precisely to prevent this. confirmedGaps.location: backend/internal/service/admin_user_service.go:283-289; backend/internal/middleware/jwt_auth.go:39-47; backend/internal/middleware/middleware.go:558-573; backend/internal/auth/auth.go:257-271
confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: An admin who impersonates a user (POST /api/v1/admin/users/{id}/impersonate, admin_routes.go:79) receives a token byte-for-byte indistinguishable from that user's real login session — full read/write. The documented 'impersonated sessions are read-only' guarantee does not exist in production. An admin can mutate a tenant's data under impersonation with no technical restriction (only the audit log records the original impersonate action, not subsequent writes as the impersonating actor).
confirmedGaps.recommendation: Add an Impersonation bool to auth.TokenClaims; thread it through GenerateAccessToken/generateAccessTokenUnlocked into the JWT map claims; set it true in ImpersonateUser; copy "impersonation" into JWTAuth's claimsMap; and mount middleware.RejectImpersonationWrites on the impersonation-capable surface in cmd/api/main.go (or wherever impersonation tokens are accepted). Then make the rbac test exercise a real ImpersonateUser-minted token rather than a hand-injected claim. If full read-write impersonation is in fact intended, delete RejectImpersonationWrites and its test to remove the misleading dead control.
confirmedGaps.refuteReasoning:
I read all four cited locations plus the full token lifecycle and confirmed every link of the chain is broken, so the "impersonated sessions are read-only" guarantee does not exist in production.

(1) MINT — admin_user_service.go:283-289: ImpersonateUser builds auth.TokenClaims{Sub, WorkspaceID, Role, PlatformRole, StateID} with NO impersonation field. The comment at :255-256 explicitly states the goal is to make the token "shape identical to a genuine login token so every downstream workspace API treats it the same" — i.e. indistinguishable from a real session by design.

(2) STRUCT — auth.go:257-271: TokenClaims has Sub/WorkspaceID/Role/PlatformRole/StateID/MFAVerified/ExpiresAt only. There is no impersonation field, so the value can never be carried.

(3) SIGN — auth.go:337-360: GenerateAccessToken writes jwt.MapClaims with sub/workspace_id/role/platform_role/state_id/mfa_verified/iss/aud/exp/iat. No impersonation claim is ever placed in the JWT body.

(4) PARSE — auth.go:362-408: ParseAccessToken reconstructs TokenClaims from sub/workspace_id/role/platform_role/state_id/mfa_verified only. Even a token that somehow carried an impersonation claim would be dropped here.

(5) PROPAGATE — jwt_auth.go:39-47: JWTAuth builds claimsMap with sub/user_id/workspace_id/role/platform_role/state_id/mfa_verified. No "impersonation" key, so RejectImpersonationWrites' lookup claims["impersonation"].(bool) is always (false, false).

(6) DELIVERY — admin_users.go:169-182: Impersonate returns {"token": token} as a plain bearer token; the client replays it through the standard JWTAuth path above, confirming no special handling that would set the claim.

(7) MOUNT — grep across the repo: RejectImpersonationWrites is referenced ONLY at tests/security/admin_rbac_test.go:162. It is NOT mounted in cmd/api/main.go (grep returned zero hits for the middleware there) nor in admin_routes.go (the /api/v1/admin group at admin_routes.go:62-141 uses only RequireAuth + RequirePlatformRole; the impersonate route is registered at :79 with no read-only guard). main.go:2092 only logs a warning if JWT_IMPERSONATION_SECRET is unset.

(8) FALSE CONFIDENCE — admin_rbac_test.go:157-187 (esp. :150-152, :171-176): the passing test hand-injects "impersonation": true directly into the claims map via requestWithClaims and mounts RejectImpersonationWrites inline in a throwaway chi router. It never exercises ImpersonateUser, GenerateAccessToken, or the real admin route wiring, so it cannot catch the broken contract.

Net effect: an admin impersonating a user (POST /api/v1/admin/users/{id}/impersonate) receives a token byte-for-byte equivalent to that user's real login (read+write), with no technical write restriction. Only the initial impersonate action is audited (admin_user_service.go:293-296); subsequent writes are attributed to the impersonated user with no impersonation marker. Severity HIGH is appropriate: it is a privilege/accountability hole within an already-privileged admin role rather than an unauthenticated tenant-isolation breach, so not CRITICAL, but the documented safety control is entirely non-functional in production.

confirmedGaps.title: user_auth_methods has no uniqueness constraint on (provider, provider_subject); LinkOAuth dedups only by exact triple, so a Google sub is not pinned to one account
confirmedGaps.location: backend/internal/database/migrations/003_create_auth.up.sql:18-23 (user_auth_methods has no UNIQUE on provider+provider_subject); backend/cmd/api/oauth_store.go:84-95 (LinkOAuth INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS only guards the full (user_id,provider,provider_subject) triple)
confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: HandleGoogleCallback resolves identity by email (FindByEmail, auth.go:722), not by provider_subject. If a Google account's primary email ever changes/reassigns, or two user rows ever share linkage, the same Google sub could become associated with more than one user row with no DB guard. Today login is email-keyed so the practical blast radius is low, but the table cannot enforce 'one Google identity → one account' and there is no index for reverse lookup by sub.
confirmedGaps.recommendation: Add a UNIQUE index on user_auth_methods(provider, provider_subject) and resolve callback identity by provider_subject first, falling back to email only for first-time linking.
confirmedGaps.refuteReasoning: Both factual claims verified. (1) user_auth_methods has NO UNIQUE constraint on (provider, provider_subject) — the table defines only id PK, user_id FK, provider, provider_subject, with no unique index; grep confirms migration 003 is the only one touching the table and no later migration adds the constraint (003_create_auth.up.sql:18-23, down.sql:1). (2) LinkOAuth dedups only on the full (user_id, provider, provider_subject) triple via WHERE NOT EXISTS, so the same Google sub CAN be inserted against multiple user_id rows with no DB guard (oauth_store.go:84-95). (3) Identity resolution in HandleGoogleCallback is purely email-keyed (FindByEmail at auth.go:722 → LinkOAuth at 728/765); a codebase-wide grep confirms provider_subject is write-only — there is NO reverse lookup by subject anywhere, so the missing index claim is also true, and OAuthProfile has no EmailVerified field (auth.go:51-56), meaning the join trusts the provider email. Mitigating context that caps severity, not a refutation: users.email is UNIQUE (002_create_users.up.sql:3), and since every account resolution path keys on email, that unique column is the de-facto 'one identity → one account' guard today. The duplicate-subject break requires the conditions the claim itself flags as hypothetical (email reassignment / pre-existing shared linkage), which no current code path can produce because email is unique and is the sole join key. So this is a real latent data-model/integrity gap (missing UNIQUE constraint + missing reverse-lookup index), correctly described, but defensive rather than an actively broken contract or live tenant-isolation hole — consistent with MEDIUM, at the low end of it.
confirmedGaps.verifyEvidence: backend/internal/database/migrations/003_create_auth.up.sql:18-23 (no UNIQUE on provider+provider_subject); backend/cmd/api/oauth_store.go:84-95 (LinkOAuth WHERE NOT EXISTS guards only the full triple); backend/internal/auth/auth.go:722,728,765 (email-keyed resolution, provider_subject write-only); backend/internal/auth/auth.go:51-56 (OAuthProfile has no EmailVerified); backend/internal/database/migrations/002_create_users.up.sql:3 (email UNIQUE — the de-facto identity guard today)

confirmedGaps.title: OAuth callback ignores Google's email_verified claim and links/logs into any pre-existing local account by email match
confirmedGaps.location: backend/internal/auth/google_provider.go:94-105 (GetProfile decodes only sub/email/name/picture — Google's email_verified is never read); backend/internal/auth/auth.go:722-744 (existing user found by email → LinkOAuth + return, no verification check)
confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: Two coupled issues. (1) The callback trusts the email without consulting Google's email_verified flag; with a Google Workspace/custom domain that returns an unverified email this could associate an unveried address. (2) If a local password account exists for that email but never completed email OTP (email_verified=FALSE in users), the Google callback links Google and issues a full session, effectively bypassing the email-OTP activation gate that password Login enforces at handler.go:446-449. This is arguably acceptable (Google asserts the email) but it is an undocumented divergence: the OAuth path has no equivalent of the 'account not activated' 403, and no code sets users.email_verified=TRUE for the Google-created/linked account either (the row stays at the DB default FALSE per migration 006), leaving an inconsistent verified state.
confirmedGaps.recommendation: Require Google's email_verified=true in GetProfile/HandleGoogleCallback before linking, and explicitly set users.email_verified=TRUE when an account is created or linked via a verified Google identity so the verified-state field is consistent across both signup paths.
confirmedGaps.refuteReasoning: Every component of the claim is verified against source. (1) GetProfile (google_provider.go:94-99) decodes only sub/email/name/picture — Google's email_verified is genuinely never requested or read; scope is "openid email profile" (auth.go:693). (2) HandleGoogleCallback (auth.go:722-744) finds an existing user purely by email match, calls LinkOAuth + BackfillProfile, and returns the user with no verification check. (3) The callback handler OAuthGoogleCallback (handler.go:716-793) then issues a full refresh token + authenticated=1 redirect; there is NO equivalent of the password Login path's 403 "account not activated" gate at handler.go:446-449. So a local password account stuck at email_verified=FALSE (blocked from password login) CAN be fully logged in via Google. (4) The inconsistent-state half is also true: oauthUserStore.Create (oauth_store.go:42-70) calls users.Create(CreateUserInput{Email:...}); CreateUserInput (user.go:45-52) has no EmailVerified field, service.Create (user.go:96-103) never sets it, and repo INSERT (user/repo.go:46-49) writes the zero value false. Neither the OAuth store nor HandleGoogleCallback ever calls MarkEmailVerified, so Google-created/linked rows persist at email_verified=FALSE — confirmed default by migration 006_add_password_to_users.up.sql:5 (NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE). I searched for any reconciliation (MarkEmailVerified is only called from the OTP verify path at handler.go:546, never from OAuth). This is a genuine integration gap between the two login paths plus a persistent data-integrity inconsistency, not a stylistic nit. Severity stays MEDIUM: it is not a tenant-isolation hole and does not break the normal-user flow, but it is an undocumented divergence (OAuth has no activation gate) and leaves authenticated users with email_verified=FALSE, which any downstream check keyed on that flag would read inconsistently. The unverified-email half (sub-claim 1) is real but low practical risk on its own (requires an attacker-controlled Workspace/custom domain).

confirmedGaps.title: Second workspace-creation path (POST /workspace) skips quota + membership co-creation, violating the lifecycle invariant
confirmedGaps.location: backend/internal/workspace/handler.go:45-79 (Create) + workspace/workspace.go:104-142 (service.Create only provisions bucket + publishes event) vs cmd/api/main.go:514-529 (only onboardingWorkspaceCreator inserts workspace_members and workspace_storage)
confirmedGaps.whatBreaks: workspace.Handler.Create is mounted and reachable at POST /workspace for any authenticated, onboarded user (cmd/api/main.go:1278), but it calls wsSvc.Create directly, which creates NO workspace_storage quota row and NO workspace_members row. A workspace born this way has the lifecycle invariant broken: the dashboard storage widget and quota enforcement fall back to plan defaults (degraded, not fatal) and AuthLookup must use its owner fallback because the membership row is absent. The frontend never calls this route (only onboarding creates workspaces), so it is an orphan/divergent API surface rather than a live-broken UI flow.
confirmedGaps.recommendation: Either remove/disable the POST /workspace route, or route it through the same adapter that co-creates workspace_members + workspace_storage so there is exactly one canonical creation path.
confirmedGaps.refuteReasoning:
The structural divergence is real: workspace.service.Create (workspace.go:104-142) only inserts the workspace row, calls bucket.ProvisionBucket, and publishes workspace.created — it inserts NO workspace_members and NO workspace_storage row. The onboarding adapter is the only caller that co-creates those (main.go:514-519 inserts workspace_members with role Owner; main.go:521-529 seeds workspace_storage from PlanDefaultQuotaBytes). workspace.Handler.Create (handler.go:45-79) calls svc.Create directly with no co-creation and is mounted at POST /workspace (main.go:1278) behind JWTAuth+TenantContext+RequireState, so it is reachable by any authenticated, onboarded user. So far the claim is accurate.

However, every downstream consequence is already handled by fallbacks — exactly as the claim itself concedes ("degraded, not fatal", "orphan/divergent API surface"). (1) Missing membership: AuthLookup.GetUserWorkspace has an explicit owner-fallback branch (auth_lookup.go:50-62) that, when no workspace_members row exists, joins workspaces on owner_id and returns role hardcoded to "Owner". So the owner is NOT locked out. (2) Missing quota row: StorageAccounting.GetUsage LEFT JOINs workspace_storage and falls back to PlanDefaultQuotaBytes(planTier) when quota_bytes==0 (storage_accounting_service.go:124-142), so the widget still shows a meaningful limit; ReserveUpload (190+) and ApplyDerivativeDelta (160-166) self-seed the row via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT on first upload; the GetUsage handler returns zeros on error rather than 500 (storage_analytics_handler.go:69-71). CheckQuota treats quota_bytes==0 as unlimited (180-181) — a brief over-permissive window until the row self-seeds, but not a hard break.

There is no security or tenant-isolation hole: TenantContext middleware still applies on POST /workspace, and GetByID enforces a cross-tenant check (handler.go:90-95). The frontend never calls bare POST /workspace (grep of frontend/src shows only /api/v1/workspace/subscription/* subresource calls; the bare handler is mounted at root /workspace, a different path than the live /api/v1/workspace subscription routes). So this is a dead/orphan API surface with self-healing degradation, not a live-broken flow or data-corruption risk. The gap is genuine but the claimed HIGH severity overstates impact — the auditor's own description (degraded, orphan) is a MEDIUM-class latent inconsistency.
